propositions: The decision_flips metric counts a gold pair as a flip whenever a.decision != b.decision without checking if either side has errored=True, treating synthetic decisions from errored records identically to model verdicts.

A single transient error on one arm (e.g., ThrottlingException) creates a fabricated flip that fails the parity gating criterion (b) 'ZERO decision-level flips', falsely registering as a model-quality regression.

The errored guard must read the errored flag directly rather than testing decision-vocabulary membership, because gold_pairs admission is gated on label membership at line 105, not decision membership.

An errored pair with errored=True and valid=True produces a silent fabricated flip with no corroborating signal in error_rate or validity metrics, making the flip indistinguishable from genuine regressions.

The same event is double-counted: once under criterion (b) as a fabricated flip and again under criterion (d) as a runtime error, when errored pairs should be excluded from flip scoring and attributed only to the error-rate criterion.
